verdict: Illumina's revenue rose 4% to $1.13B and GAAP net income jumped to $220M — though an expected $79M tariff refund flattered costs; without the refund effects, operating profit was $292M.

segments.name: Product revenue
segments.note: Gene-sequencing machines and the consumable kits each run uses — placements of the high-end NovaSeq X were robust in the quarter.

segments.name: Service & other revenue
segments.note: Service contracts, maintenance and other services for the installed base of sequencers.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing the next sequencers, chemistry and analysis software.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling to labs and hospitals, plus the back office.

otherDetail: Interest and other non-operating items, net — a $41M net cost this quarter.

takeaways.title: Clinical demand drove the beat
takeaways.text: Revenue of $1.13B grew 4% and came in above guidance on healthy clinical demand and strong NovaSeq X placements; service revenue grew 17%.

takeaways.title: A refund is inside the profit
takeaways.text: Expected IEEPA tariff refunds added a $79M benefit inside cost of revenue (and cut revenue by $37M for customer credits). Excluding them, operating profit was $292M, not $305M.

takeaways.title: Cash generation improved
takeaways.text: Free cash flow rose to $378M from $253M a year ago, and Illumina raised full-year guidance: revenue of $4.64–4.66B and non-GAAP EPS of $5.40–$5.45.

oneTimers: Expected refunds of IEEPA tariffs: a $79M benefit recognized as a reduction of cost of revenue, and a $37M reduction of revenue for the portion expected to be credited back to customers. Excluding both, revenue was $1.166B, operating profit $292M and non-GAAP EPS $1.44.
footerNote: GAAP figures include the expected IEEPA tariff-refund effects described in the one-time items box.
